newsitem.title: CANADA: Growth stalls in Canada's key export sector.
newsitem.headline: Growth stalls in Canada's key export sector.

text.p: Canada's export growth, which has been the engine of the country's economic recovery, has stalled after more than a year of steady gains.
For the fourth month in a row, exports in May were almost flat at C$24.5 billion ($17.8 billion), according to data released on Friday by the Statistics Canada federal agency.
Exports, which helped pull Canada out of recession in the early 1990s, account for about 37 percent of the nation's gross domestic product -- the highest level of any G7 country.

Economists said the recent trade numbers would likely mean a widening of the current account deficit, but an expected surge in domestic demand should push up GDP this year despite the slowdown in trade growth.
The plateau in exports "suggests that the trade situation will be less support for growth than it has in the past," said Craig Wright, deputy chief economist at Royal Bank of Canada.

The trade surplus inched up in May to C$2 billion ($1.45 billion) from a 2-1/2-year low of C$1.7 billion ($1.2 billion) in April. The surplus has been slipping down since peaking at C$4.3 billion ($3.1 billion) in August 1996.

"After a record shattering performance in 1996, Canada's trade surplus is having difficulty pulling out of a recent funk," economist Sherry Cooper at brokerage Nesbitt Burns said in a statement. "The smaller surpluses this year are a function of both blazing imports...and more subdued export gains."
Imports fell 1.6 percent in May to C$22.5 billion ($16.4 billion) after rising 3.8 percent in April, Statistics Canada said.
A spokeswoman for Canada's Trade Minister Sergio Marchi said the government was not worried about the stalled growth in exports and the slimmer trade balances.
"They (exports) are still at record high levels," said spokeswoman Leslie Swartman. "These numbers are still quite high."
Canada has made clear that the main thrust of its trade policy is to diversify its export markets away from reliance on the huge U.S. market.

Canada and the United States have the world's biggest trading partnership. Canada sent exports worth C$20 billion ($14.5 billion) to the United States in May, and imported goods and services worth C$17.2 billion ($12.5 billion).

Despite the Canadian government's efforts, trade balances with Japan, the European Union and other countries belonging to the Organization of Economic Cooperation and Development have slipped in the past three months.

Canada plans to send a trade delegation -- including Prime Minister Jean Chretien, provincial premiers and business leaders -- to Latin America in January to help boost trade opportunities there, a government spokesman said.
